cohort: The study included 499 primigravid women aged <=19 years admitted for delivery, abortion, or medical termination of pregnancy at the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at Tirunelveli Govt Medical College.
finding: Teenage pregnancy was associated with significant maternal and neonatal risks, including high rates of anaemia, hypertensive disorders, increased caesarean deliveries, and various neonatal complications such as low birth weight, preterm birth, and increased neonatal mortality, with morbidity significantly linked to younger maternal age and poor nutritional status.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate was 29.4%, with cephalopelvic disproportion accounting for 31.8% of these cases.
cross-section timing: Observations were recorded for women admitted between November 2019 to November 2021 at the time of delivery, abortion, or medical termination of pregnancy.
birth_weight: Not specified for all participants, but low birth weight (<2.5 kg) was an outcome affecting 34.9% of newborns.
gest_age: Not specified for all participants, but preterm birth was an outcome affecting 25.5% of newborns.
